note:
A CAMPAIGN CANNOT EXERCISE A CHANGE TO THE CHAMBER'S OWN DRIVER THROUGH THE CHAMBER. Found by campaign/the-spillway, sharpened here after reading the code, because the boundary is not where either of us first assumed.

THEIR OBSERVATION: the drain runs sluice-census.sh from the queue CHECKOUT's scripts/, so a campaign changing the delivery script gets a run whose log lacks its change. Correct, and it cost them a planned production proof -- they have correctly re-recorded the proof as "the first census AFTER merge".

THE EXACT BOUNDARY, from scripts/sluice-run.sh:

    line 502   lane_sets_file="${HV_SLUICE_LANE_SETS:-$repo_root/scripts/lane-sets.tsv}"   <- CHECKOUT
    line 769   cd "$wt"                                                                    <- phases run in the WORKTREE

So three different answers depending on what you changed:

  - THE DRIVER (sluice-run.sh, sluice-census.sh, sluice-drain.sh): comes from the checkout. Your change does NOT run. Proof is the first job after merge.
  - THE ROSTER (scripts/lane-sets.tsv): read from the CHECKOUT even though it names the phases. Your change to WHICH phases run, or to their commands as written in the TSV, does NOT take effect for your own job.
  - A PHASE SCRIPT (lane-outboard.sh, and anything a phase command invokes relatively): executes with cwd = the merge-product worktree, so YOUR version runs. Your change IS exercised.

That third one is the useful half: it means a campaign changing lane-outboard.sh, test-sluice.sh or a gate script does get tested by its own edit, and only driver/roster changes have the bootstrap gap.

A SECOND CONSEQUENCE NOBODY HAS BEEN TRACKING, and I only looked because the same session caught my checkout being stale. Because the roster is read from $repo_root, THE CHAMBER RUNS WHATEVER ROSTER THE CHECKOUT HAPPENS TO HOLD. A main checkout that has drifted behind means jobs are gated against an older phase list than the merge product declares, silently. I checked my own window: my checkout sat at b71296a8a while origin/main reached fd7f1d4f4, and `git log b71296a8a..fd7f1d4f4 -- scripts/lane-sets.tsv` is EMPTY, so nothing was mis-gated. That is luck, not design -- the roster did change three times during The Governor's 0426 work, and a stale checkout across one of those commits would have run the wrong phase list with no signal at all.

OPERATOR RULE that follows: fast-forward the main checkout before draining, not merely when something looks wrong. The mouth no longer depends on it (its classifier reads refs now), but the ROSTER still does, and that dependency is silent in both directions.
